summary: Constellation answers in support of PJM's abeyance motion with one clarification: PJM must still file complete Interim NITS provisions on August 17, 2026 in the co-location docket, and may handle Contract Demand Services on a separate track.
ask: Grant PJM's abeyance motion with a clarification that PJM's obligation to file full Interim NITS provisions by August 17, 2026 in the co-location proceeding is unchanged.

points.point: Constellation supports abeyance on the condition that PJM still files a complete set of Interim NITS provisions on August 17, 2026.
points.quote: PJM remains obligated to file on August 17, 2026, a complete set of provisions to facilitate Interim Network Integration Transmission Service (“NITS”), that will allow for a prompt start of service.

points.point: Constellation says Contract Demand Services may need up to 90 more days while Interim NITS is basically NITS.
points.quote: developing the terms and conditions for Contract Demand Services may require an additional 90 days.

points.point: It asks FERC to require PJM to reconsider its proposed June 1, 2029 Interim NITS effective date.
points.quote: Reconsider its proposed June 1, 2029 effective date given that the interconnection of large loads is an “urgent” issue

points.point: Constellation says the two proceedings have distinct compliance obligations that PJM must not conflate.
points.quote: they are separate proceedings with distinct compliance obligations that PJM must not conflate

throughLine.text: Answer on PJM's E-7 abeyance motion that insists the E-2 Interim NITS compliance proceed on schedule while the E-7 flexible load service work is deferred.
